newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich falls after first share auction.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich falls after first share auction.

text.p: Shares in Woolwich Plc fell on Tuesday after the first auction of shares in the former building society saw 92.55 million shares sold at a discount of more than 5 percent to Monday's closing price, dealers said.
Woolwich shares, which made their market debut on Monday, dropped 24p to 310p by 0738 GMT.
Woolwich said on Tuesday shares in the auction were sold at an average price of 315.35p per share, compared to the closing price on Monday of 334p.

Dealers said the stock had reached an artificially high level on Monday as market-makers had driven up the price to attract small, retail sellers and to avoid being caught short of stock by potentially strong demand from institutions.
The fall in Woolwich also weighed on other former building societies turned banks. Shares in Abbey National Plc dropped 16p to 860-1/2p and Alliance & Leicester Plc slipped six anew to 607p.
Analysts said Woolwich shares still looked over-priced, even after the fall on Tuesday.
"If you look at the stock's rating against fundamentals, it still looks too expensive," said one analyst at a leading securities house.
